clue.text: Two pieces of tableware put into the window

parts.note: a plate is an item of tableware
a glass is also an item of tableware, the second of the two pieces

explanation.surface: Someone sets two items of crockery on the windowsill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two pieces of tableware' gives both pieces: a dish and a drinking vessel, side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Large thick sheets of this material are used to glaze shop fronts, so it stands for a window.

clue.text: Circle around the pond

indicators.note: around means the word for the pond is turned back to front

parts.note: a pool is a pond

explanation.surface: Walk in a circle around the pond.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring or circle of string or path forms this shape.

clue.text: An article to veto on old Egyptian

parts.note: the is the definite article
to ban is to veto

explanation.surface: A piece of writing proposes banning something to do with an ancient Egyptian.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhabitant of ancient Thebes on the Nile was an Egyptian of old.

clue.text: First astronaut is senile, but comes right in the end

parts.note: gaga means senile
taken as written

explanation.surface: A space pioneer is going doddery but recovers at the last.
explanation.walkthrough: Yuri Gagarin was the first person in space, in 1961.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet cosmonaut was the first human to orbit the Earth.

clue.text: Crooked supply of a whisky reported

indicators.note: reported says the words a whisky are judged as they sound when spoken

parts.note: a rye, rye being a kind of whisky

explanation.surface: Someone describes a dodgy supply of whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Askew or bent out of line means crooked.

clue.text: Lies disastrously about ship heading east — it's stationary

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters surround the next pieces
disastrously suggests the letters of lies go badly wrong and are rearranged
heading says east comes before ship

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A ship heading east is surrounded by terrible lies and goes nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disastrously' makes SILE; 'about' wraps it round ESS, with east 'heading' the ship. The definition is the botanical sense: attached without a stalk.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology, attached directly at the base and not free to move means stationary.

clue.text: Mortifying to discover terrible rage nuns go into

indicators.note: terrible suggests the letters of rage nuns go are badly mixed up

explanation.surface: Discovering the nuns flying into an awful rage is embarrassing.
explanation.definitionFit: Mortifying in the medical sense is tissue dying and decaying.

clue.text: A colourful way to make one's point when disapproving?

definitions.text: A colourful way to make one's point when disapproving?

parts.words: A colourful way to make one's point when disapproving?
parts.note: an editor's coloured writing tool, whose point marks cuts in text that is disapproved of

explanation.definitionFit: Editors and censors traditionally strike out material with this tool, so it means to censor.

clue.text: Cover-up that may become tedious

definitions.meaning: a cloth spread over a coffin

explanation.surface: A cover-up story that might start to bore people.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a funeral cloth covering a coffin; the verb means to grow wearisome.

clue.text: Insurance for women — they work as models

parts.note: insurance protection is called cover
girls is an informal word for women

explanation.surface: An insurance policy designed for women in the fashion business.
explanation.definitionFit: Magazine front pages feature photographic models, so these women earn a living posing.

clue.text: Lacking a partner, has to sing Leo's part

indicators.note: part says only a portion of the words sing Leo's is taken

explanation.surface: A soloist without a duet partner is told to sing the role of Leo.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unmarried or unattached is without a partner.

clue.text: Very worried — can rift be mended?

indicators.note: mended suggests the letters of can rift are repaired into a new order

explanation.surface: An anxious person wonders whether a quarrel can be patched up.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenzied and desperate with anxiety is a synonym for extremely worried.

clue.text: Take it from one mug to another — in person!

parts.note: mug is slang for face
another mug, so another face

explanation.surface: Advice on moving a drink from one cup to the next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' here is slang for the face, not a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Meeting directly with the other person present means in person.

clue.text: They'll surface when air-bus carries sex symbol to the French

indicators.note: carries means the aircraft name holds the following pieces inside

parts.note: taken as written, without the hyphen
BB, Brigitte Bardot, the French film star and sex symbol
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An aircraft carries a famous actress to France.
explanation.walkthrough: BB is Brigitte Bardot, a 1950s-60s French screen sex symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Pockets of gas in a liquid rise and appear at the top.

clue.text: Seen, heard and named

indicators.note: heard says the word for seen counts as it sounds

parts.note: sighted means seen

explanation.surface: Someone was observed, overheard and identified.
explanation.definitionFit: Mentioned by name, as in a citation, is the meaning.

clue.text: East European finding affection in most quarters

indicators.note: in says the word for affection sits inside the compass points

parts.note: three of the four compass quarters: south, north and east
love is affection

explanation.surface: A traveller from eastern Europe finds kindness almost everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most quarters' is three of the four compass points, S, N and E; LOVE goes after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Slovenia is from eastern Europe.

clue.text: Writing, but no time to finish off screenplay

indicators.note: no time means the abbreviation for time is dropped from the word for screenplay

parts.note: a script is a screenplay

explanation.surface: A writer with no time to finish the screenplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A certificate or written document, as in scrip money, is a form of writing.

clue.text: Pleasant to have English family connection

indicators.note: to have means the word for pleasant holds the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: It is nice to have English relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a relative, that is a family connection.

clue.text: A joker who needs keeping in hand?

definitions.meaning: a joker or wag, an amusing character
a playing ... is held in the hand during a game

explanation.surface: A prankster who has to be kept under control.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric wit is called this, and a playing card is held in your hand.

clue.text: Last letter is nothing, when in charge of animals

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone in charge of animals says the last letter is nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to animal life, as in zoology.

clue.text: Danger for a fairy reaching 50

parts.note: a peri is a fairy of Persian legend
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A fairy turning fifty faces hazards.
explanation.walkthrough: A PERI is a fairy in Persian mythology, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril is a synonym for danger or jeopardy.

clue.text: Hanging onto the writer, an Italian poet losing energy

parts.note: a pen is the tool that writes

indicators.note: losing means one letter is dropped from the poet's name

parts.note: Dante is the Italian poet

explanation.surface: Clinging to the author, an Italian poet runs out of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pendent, suspended or dangling, means hanging; the jewellery noun hangs from a chain.

clue.text: Reading a speech

definitions.meaning: a reading or reprimand delivered aloud

explanation.surface: A reading delivered as a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal talk to students is a talk, and a university reading is the same thing.

clue.text: Tied up support for journalist

parts.note: a truss is a supporting frame or surgical support
ED, short for editor, is a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter is bound with a supporting strap.
explanation.definitionFit: Trussed means bound tightly, as a chicken before roasting.

clue.text: Scrutiny of south American state's aluminium production

parts.note: Peru is a South American country, and the 's adds an S
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: An inspection of aluminium production in a South American country.
explanation.definitionFit: A careful reading through or examination is scrutiny.

clue.text: Inexperienced peacekeepers may be taken advantage of

parts.note: UN, the United Nations, provides peacekeepers
used means exploited

explanation.surface: Green peacekeeping troops may be exploited.
explanation.definitionFit: Not accustomed to something, or new and fresh, matches inexperienced.

clue.text: Mythical tale with a sad end

parts.note: a fable is a tale

indicators.note: end picks the final letter of the word sad

explanation.surface: A legendary story with an unhappy ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrated in legend means mythical.

clue.text: It may make it difficult to see, yet sun is out

definitions.text: It may make it difficult to see

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for sun or Sunday

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: Glare may still blind you, even though the sun is out.
explanation.definitionFit: A swelling on the eyelid can impair vision.

clue.text: Topple aristocratic old sultan in India

parts.note: to tip is to topple
U means upper-class, aristocratic

explanation.surface: An ancient Indian ruler topples the aristocracy.
explanation.walkthrough: Tipu Sultan ruled Mysore in the 18th century; U is the old label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipu was an 18th-century ruler of Mysore in southern India.

clue.text: Unselfish liars? Cut it out!

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of liars and cut it are knocked out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone exasperated tells dishonest people to stop lying.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting others first is the selfless quality of the word.

clue.text: The main, but not the one, caterer

indicators.note: but not means a letter is to be left out of the word for main

parts.note: the main one is the chief
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The head caterer, but not the one in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook who prepares meals professionally caters for people.

clue.text: In a delirium, do you hear it? Terrific!

indicators.note: In tells us the following pieces go inside the delirium word

parts.note: tremens, from delirium tremens, the shakes of alcohol withdrawal
taken as written

indicators.note: hear says the word you is taken as it sounds, a single letter

parts.note: you sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: Someone in a drunken delirium asks if you can hear something wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: TREMENS stands for delirium tremens; DO and U go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous or excellent, both meanings of terrific.
